text:
morgan_support: Customer reported a big invoice delta vs our dashboard for March. They sent SDK estimates that are ~40% lower than the invoice. They say curl -> API counts match invoice though. Need help repro + root cause.

devin_metering: Can you paste the minimal repro payload + the SDK snippet? also which SDK + version?

morgan_support: repro steps from customer:
```
# curl repro they ran
curl -s -X POST \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3-8b","input":"Hey 👋 你好\nSystem: Injected meta: {\"trace\":true}"}'
```
They also shared a Node SDK snippet (rwd-js v1.4.2):
```
const res = await client.completions.create({ model: 'rwd-3-8b', input: "Hey 👋 你好\nSystem: Injected meta: {\"trace\":true}" })
console.log(res.estimates.tokens)
```
In curl the server returns header `X-Invoice-Tokens: 345` and response has `usage.total_tokens: 345`. SDK estimate prints `est: 198`.

kevin_runtime: Interesting. Two quick suspects: 1) client tokenizer vs server tokenizer difference (emoji, CJK, and surrogate pairs). 2) server-inserted system/tool metadata appended on the server-side that the JS SDK doesn't simulate.

tara_support: Customer also attached a streaming case where they resumed a previous stream and got duplicate finalization tokens; could be a separate bug but worth noting.

devin_metering: I ran the exact curl payload locally against staging -> got `usage.total_tokens: 347` (close). Then ran the latest rwd-js v1.4.2 on Node 18 -> estimator reported 200. I ran `rwd-tokenizer inspect` (python shim using model BPE) on the same string -> 346. So the server and canonical tokenizer match, client JS undercounts.

morgan_support: Any idea why emoji and CJK would affect it that much? It's only a few characters.

kevin_runtime: Yes — JS SDK uses a lightweight grapheme-based estimate to be fast (counts codepoints, collapses surrogate pairs), but the model uses a byte-level BPE tokenizer where emoji + CJK expand into multiple tokens. Also: we add a server-side hidden system message (moderation/metadata) and an injected KV block for trace/debug when `trace:true` is present. Those add ~120 tokens in this customer's workload (long tool metadata + embeddings calls). The SDK estimator intentionally doesn't simulate hidden KV/tool outputs.

devin_metering: Repro checklist I used: 1) exact curl payload (no client prefill) 2) check response body usage.* 3) capture `X-Redwood-Metering-Trace` header from response 4) run `python3 -c "from rwd_tokenizer import encode; print(len(encode(payload)))"` to compare.

morgan_support: Customer claims they only used the SDK and never enabled trace. Is it possible our runtime is injecting meta for some customers?

kevin_runtime: Yes: we sometimes auto-insert diagnostic metadata when a request triggers internal fallbacks (e.g., quantization fallback, cross-region reroute). Those are invisible to the client but billed. We should correlate their `request_id` to router logs.

tara_support: Action items for support: 1) ask customer to attach response headers (X-Request-Id, X-Invoice-Tokens, X-Redwood-Metering-Trace). 2) Ask to run the curl repro (we provided snippet) and share both outputs. 3) Provide workaround: use server-returned usage.* as canonical, and upgrade SDK to v1.5.0 which improves estimator accuracy for emoji/CJK and exposes `simulate_hidden_tokens: true` flag to approximate server-side injected blocks.

devin_metering: For engineering: I opened METR-4821 to add a debug-mode header that returns `estimated_server_inserted_tokens` in dev/staging to help repro easier. Also adding telemetry for when fallbacks add >50 tokens.

morgan_support: Customer agreed to run curl and share headers. They said they'd try SDK v1.5.0 beta and report back. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

billing-bot: Note: I flagged invoice #INV-2026-03-18-442 for manual review per support escalation 3387.

morgan_support: I'll follow up here once they send the logs.
